endpoint.name: google.serp.organic — routed: best of 7 providers, own keys first
endpoint.summary: Google organic results for a keyword — provider-native result rows in `results`; `limit` is the depth

cost.note: NOT free: misses are billed too. the children's range $0.00015–$0.015 per hit, 0% markup; you pay the child that served AND every child tried before it that bills a miss (3 of 7 do), up to X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost (default $1 a call). X-Treg-Route-Exclude them, or X-Treg-Route-Waterfall: 0, to pay for one provider only

country.note: filter — default 'us'; ISO country code; mapped to each provider's location code / gl / region

limit.note: filter — default 10; results to return where the provider bills by depth

input.note: Send everything you know about the subject — treg derives the rest (full_name ⇄ first+last), matches each provider on the variants it accepts ({q} | {ai_overview, q}) and sends each provider only the fields it wants. On a miss treg keeps trying providers, cheapest first, within X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost (default $1 per call; misses on per-success providers are free). Options ride as headers, never in the body: X-Treg-Route-Waterfall: 0 (stop at the first miss), X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost: <usd>, X-Treg-Route-Prefer / X-Treg-Route-Exclude: <provider>. The response is {output, raw, _treg: {served_by, tried}}; X-Treg-Served-By names the child.

siblings.name: Google Search
siblings.summary: Run a Google web search and get the organic results (title, link, snippet, position) as clean JSON. Returns about 10 results per call - Google stopped honoring bulk result counts in September 2025, so a limit above 10 is accepted but returns no more than a page. Send page 2, 3, ... to walk further, or use google.search_100 for up to 100 ranked results in one call, which is cheaper past roughly 20 results.
siblings.call_template: treg call anyapi.google.serp.organic --method POST --data '{"query":"best coffee maker","limit":1}'

autocorrect.note: Toggle Google spelling autocorrect (default true). Set false to search the exact query without correction.

cursor.note: Deprecated: send page instead. A continuation token from an earlier response's nextCursor is still accepted and still continues on the source that issued it; page is ignored when cursor is sent alongside it.

gl.note: Two-letter country code for result localization (e.g. us, gb, de).

hl.note: Two-letter interface and results language code (e.g. en, es, de).

limit.note: Page size to ask for. Google returns about 10 organic results per page and stopped honoring larger counts in September 2025, so a limit above 10 still returns about 10. Some sources return their whole page of about 10 whatever limit says: a page is never trimmed after the call, so nextCursor always continues exactly where this response ended. To go deeper, send page (about 10 results per page, each billed as a request) or use google.search_100, which returns up to 100 ranked results in a single call for one flat charge and is cheaper past roughly 20 results. Price is flat per request.

location.note: Fine-grained location for result localization, given as a canonical Google location string (e.g. 'New York, United States', 'London, United Kingdom'). More specific than the country-level gl.

page.note: Which page of about 10 organic results to return, starting at 1. Send page 2, 3, ... to walk deeper; each page is billed as one request and any source can serve any page. Replaces cursor.

timeframe.note: Restrict results to a recent time window: 1h, 1d, 7d, 1y, or all. Default all (no time restriction).

siblings.name: Google SERP — organic, PAA, local pack, AI Overview

siblings.call_template: treg call cloro.google.serp.organic --method POST --data '{"query":"what is a stock split","gl":"US","pages":1,"include":{"html":true,"aioverview":true,"paaAioverview":true,"googleGoto":true}}'

cost.note: 7 = 3 base + 2 for include.aioverview / paaAioverview + the 2-credit sync surcharge, for one page. A plain call without the AI Overview flags is 5. html and googleGoto are free. Each page past the first adds 2, and `pages` is capped at 10, so 23 is the ceiling. A failed extraction is not charged.

query.note: the keyword. Pass query or url, not both.

url.note: a complete google.com/search URL used as the fetch target instead of the structured fields. The URL owns query, location, uule and pages.

gl.note: result geography, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Required in structured mode; derived from the URL's gl otherwise. `country` is a deprecated alias.

location.note: free-text location; mutually exclusive with uule

uule.note: Google UULE location string; mutually exclusive with location

pages.note: 1-10, default 1. Each page past the first adds 2 credits.

include.note: any of html, aioverview, paaAioverview, googleGoto. html and googleGoto are free; aioverview or paaAioverview adds 2 credits.

siblings.name: Google organic results with true rank and page blocks

cost.note: treg's account price: 0.15 credits per Google page of 10 results, so num=30 costs 0.45; a 4xx or 5xx is free. The hold is one page; the x-c4-cost header settles the actual charge (0.150 for num=10 and 0.450 for num=30 observed live 2026-10-09).

language.note: Google interface language (hl), e.g. en or pt-br; default en

location.note: a city or region, e.g. Austin, TX; an unknown place answers 400 with the closest names

num.note: results to return: a multiple of 10 from 10 to 100 (num/10 Google pages); default 10

source.note: auto (default) may answer from Crawl4AI's fallback page, which has no AI Overview; google answers from Google's own page only, with the AI Overview when Google shows one, and is a free 503 when Google cannot be reached

siblings.name: Search Google
siblings.summary: Returns a Google results page as JSON: organic results plus every other result group Google served, such as ads, AI Overview, knowledge graph, and local results

cost.note: One successful API response consumes one prepaid call; failures are free.

fast_mode.note: Set true to return only organic_results, search_metadata, and search_parameters, skipping AI Overview and all other result groups. Only lowercase true or false are accepted.

q.note: Search query, up to 2,048 characters. Required unless ludocid or kgmid is supplied.

ludocid.note: Decimal Google CID for a local entity search. Can replace q.

kgmid.note: Google Knowledge Graph machine ID, such as /m/0k8z. Can replace q.

location.note: Human-readable search location, up to 512 characters. Use only one of location, uule, or lat and lon.

uule.note: Pre-encoded Google location token, up to 2,048 characters. Use only one of location, uule, or lat and lon.

lat.note: Latitude between -90 and 90. Supply with lon; conflicts with location and uule.

lon.note: Longitude between -180 and 180. Supply with lat; conflicts with location and uule.

radius.note: Search radius in meters around location or lat and lon, which it requires. 1 to 199 on desktop, 1 to 1,000 on tablet or mobile.

lsig.note: Opaque Google local or Knowledge Graph signature, up to 4,096 characters.

si.note: Opaque cached Google search context, up to 4,096 characters.

ibp.note: Google layout or expansion control, up to 4,096 characters.

uds.note: Opaque Google filter token, up to 4,096 characters.

color_scheme.note: Google's light or dark result presentation.

google_domain.note: A Google domain from Google's supported list, such as google.com or google.co.uk.

gl.note: Lowercase two-letter country code used to localize results.

hl.note: Google interface and result language, such as en, en-US, or de. Defaults to en.

cr.note: Country restriction: one or more countryXX values joined with |, such as countryUS.

lr.note: Language restriction: one or more lang_xx values joined with |, such as lang_en.

device.note: Google returns its real layout for the selected device: desktop, tablet, or mobile.

tbs.note: Google search-filter string, such as qdr:w, up to 4,096 characters.

safe.note: Google adult-content filtering: active or off.

nfpr.note: Set 1 to disable Google spelling auto-correction, or 0 to allow it.

pws.note: Google personalization flag: 0 or 1. 0 asks for non-personalized results.

peek_pws.note: Google personalization companion flag: 0 or 1, forwarded to Google unchanged.

tbm.note: Google vertical: lcl, vid, nws, shop, or pts. Google Images (isch) is rejected with 400 unsupported_search_vertical.

start.note: Result offset for pagination. Defaults to 0.

num.note: Requested result count, 1 to 10. A best-effort hint: Google may return fewer rows, and results are never padded.

as_dt.note: Include (i) or exclude (e) the as_sitesearch host. Requires as_sitesearch.

as_epq.note: Exact phrase the results must contain, up to 2,048 characters.

as_eq.note: Words the results must not contain, up to 2,048 characters.

as_lq.note: Return pages that link to this complete HTTP(S) URL.

as_nlo.note: Lower bound of a number range. Supply with as_nhi.

as_nhi.note: Upper bound of a number range. Supply with as_nlo.

as_oq.note: Additional terms of which any may match, up to 2,048 characters.

as_q.note: Additional terms that must all match, up to 2,048 characters.

as_qdr.note: Date range: d, w, m, or y with an optional positive count, such as m3 for the past three months.

as_rq.note: Return pages related to this complete HTTP(S) URL.

as_sitesearch.note: Hostname to include or exclude, such as example.com. A hostname, not a URL.

oq.note: Original query text from a Google URL, up to 2,048 characters; forwarded unchanged.

gs_lp.note: Opaque Google autocomplete-session value from a Google URL, up to 4,096 characters; forwarded unchanged.

sclient.note: Google client label such as gws-wiz-serp: up to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores, or hyphens.

timeout.note: Optional budget for the entire request in seconds, measured from gateway receipt until the response is ready to send. Includes admission, queueing and settlement. Must be greater than 0 and at most 90. On expiry, the call is not billed and returns 503 request_deadline_exceeded with retryable=true and a request ID. Omit to retain the standard server deadline.

siblings.name: Google organic results by keyword — top 100 domains, URLs

siblings.call_template: treg call semrush.google.serp.organic --query type=phrase_organic --query phrase=seo --query database=us

cost.note: 10 API units per LINE returned (50 units per line for historical data). One ranking URL = one line, so a full top-100 pull costs 1,000 units.

phrase.note: the keyword whose SERP you want

display_limit.note: COST DIAL — one line per ranking URL; 10 gives the first page of results

display_date.note: YYYYMM15 for a past month; historical requests bill at 50 units/line

export_columns.note: default Dn,Ur,Fk,Fp. Dn=ranking domain, Ur=ranking URL, Fk=SERP features present, Fp=SERP features the URL occupies

input.note:
CSV response. This is Semrush's DATABASE view of the SERP, not a live scrape — positions come
from Semrush's last crawl of that keyword in that regional database, so it is cheaper and
faster than a live SERP API but can lag by days. Use a live SERP provider when freshness matters.

siblings.name: Google organic search results for a query
siblings.summary: Live Google organic results for a keyword — position, title, URL, snippet, by location

cost.note: 1 search. $0.015 at the entry-level paid Developer plan ($75 / 5,000 searches); $0.010 on Production, $0.025 on Starter. Failed and cached searches are free.

engine.note: the engine selector — must be this literal string

q.note: the search query; Google search operators work here

location.note: city-level origin of the search, e.g. "Austin, Texas, United States". Mutually exclusive with uule and with lat/lon

uule.note: Google's encoded location, as an alternative to `location`

lat.note: latitude; requires lon and a matching gl

radius.note: metres around lat/lon; 1-199 on desktop, 1-1000 on mobile

gl.note: country code for the search, e.g. us, uk

cr.note: restrict to countries, e.g. countryUS; multiple joined by |

lr.note: restrict to languages, e.g. lang_en; multiple joined by |

start.note: result offset for pagination — 0, 10, 20 … This is how you page; see the note about `num`

tbm.note: switches the Google vertical: isch (images), vid, nws, shop, lcl, pts

tbs.note: advanced Google filters, e.g. date range

nfpr.note: 1 disables Google's auto-correction to a different spelling

filter.note: 0 turns off Google's similar-results and omitted-results filters

input.note:
Answers arrive in `organic_results`; the same response may also carry `knowledge_graph`,
`local_results`, `related_questions`, `related_searches` and `pagination`.
`num` IS NOT DOCUMENTED for this engine — Google dropped it upstream and SerpApi's google
parameter list does not include it. Page with `start`, not `num`; sending `num` is not a
supported way to widen a page.
